title: Jazz meant nothing to him; ballpark bands and the Pelicans
summary: Jazz did not offend him. He recalls a Black band at the ballpark on Sundays in the 1920s playing Maryland roll call, big crowds, and the Pelicans rallies.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: So jazz has actually meant absolutely nothing in my life in my musical experience. It's meant nothing to me. On the other hand, it has never I have never felt that it offended me. See what I mean? That way you can pull your hair out over the screeches of Mr. Presley in that raucous school of so-called entertainment. Heck, I liked it. We used to go at the ballpark, for example, the old days, the baseball park. I remember going back in the 1926, 27, and every Sunday at the Double Heaven, they'd have a band in the Niger Bleaches. And they'd play that Maryland roll call, that, di, da, da, da, da, da, da. And man, the crowd go crazy. You have 10, 15, 80, 10 white people they would really like. Sure, everybody loved it. Every time the Pelicans throw on a rally or the full Pelicans come to back, they'd give a couple of these fanfares and go off into it. That
